question: Should OpenClaw accept Android-side device control plus ADB or dynamic Kotlin execution as Android node commands, and which parts must be default-off, approval-gated, or handled through a broader node-registered tools contract?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix: it can grant agents phone control, file/process/log access, and arbitrary code execution on a connected Android device.

options.title: Split and security-design first
options.body: Keep this issue open, define narrow command contracts and policy gates separately, and route generic dynamic tool registration through the related node-registered tools design before implementation.

options.title: Limit to explicit Android controls
options.body: Accept a smaller device.control scope such as brightness, volume, and vibration while declining arbitrary ADB or Kotlin execution for now.

options.title: Keep dynamic execution outside core
options.body: Decline Android in-app ADB/dynamic execution in core and require an external node host, plugin, or future ClawHub package once the necessary API exists.

recommendation.title: Split and security-design first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, define narrow command contracts and policy gates separately, and route generic dynamic tool registration through the related node-registered tools design before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is mainly the node execution and model-visible tool security boundary, where steipete has the clearest adjacent ownership signal.
